comments.author: github-actions
comments.body:
Agentic Code Reviewer opencode

⚠️ **WARNING:** Step 6.3 instructs running `configure_autoload.py --write-root-agents`, and that command unconditionally overwrites the consumer's repo-root `AGENTS.md`. The script has no existence check, no backup, no marker detection, and no `--force` requirement — it replaces whatever is at `AGENTS.md` with the 26-line thin template. The interview gate makes "Refresh" the recommended default even when the existing root `AGENTS.md` is a hand-authored file (like this repo's own 400+ line harness contract), so accepting the recommended option silently destroys custom content with no way to recover it. This contradicts the harness contract that root consumer files are never overwritten by tooling and that root seeds must be create-if-missing only. When the existing file is not the generated thin pointer, the gate should default to "Keep current" and the script should refuse to clobber unless the target is a known generated file (marker comment) or `--force` is passed, with a `.bak` copy as a safety net.

**Correção sugerida:**

```diff
# configure_autoload.py — write_root_agents()
     dest = repo_root / "AGENTS.md"
+    GENERATED_MARKER = "<!-- generated by configure_autoload.py -->"
+    if dest.exists():
+        existing = dest.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
+        if GENERATED_MARKER not in existing and not force:
+            raise SystemExit(
+                "ERROR: root AGENTS.md exists and is not the generated thin pointer; "
+                "pass --force to overwrite (a .bak copy is written)"
+            )
+        if force and GENERATED_MARKER not in existing:
+            shutil.copy2(dest, dest.with_suffix(".md.bak"))
     body = ROOT_AGENTS_TEMPLATE.format(table="\n".join(table_lines))
+    body = GENERATED_MARKER + "\n" + body
```
Also flip the gate default in `INTERVIEW.md` line 74: when the existing root `AGENTS.md` lacks the generated marker, default to **Keep current** (only offer Refresh when the file is the generated thin pointer).

<details>
<summary>🔍 Detalhes da Análise IA</summary>

**Score:** 6/10 | **Ação dev:** fix-code

**Análise:**
1. Evidence: `.agents/skills/ws-configure-project/scripts/configure_autoload.py` `write_root_agents()` (lines 184-216) does `dest = repo_root / "AGENTS.md"` then unconditional `dest.write_text(body, ...)` with no `dest.exists()` check, no backup, and no `--force` gate; `INTERVIEW.md` line 74 sets "Root `AGENTS.md` present → Refresh (**Recommended**)"; `SKILL.md` line 58 gates Generate/Refresh as the recommended option; this repo's own root `AGENTS.md` is a large hand-authored harness file that would be replaced. 2. Scenario: consumer with a custom root `AGENTS.md` runs `/ws-configure-project --section autoload`, accepts the Recommended Refresh, and the script truncates and replaces their file; original content is unrecoverable (no `.bak`, no git staging). 3. Protection: the user-gate asks for consent, but the default recommendation is Refresh regardless of file authorship and the script is directly invokable by agents per step 6.3, so nothing prevents accidental loss; `ws-shared/AGENTS.md` and root `AGENTS.md` both state the installer/tooling never writes root `AGENTS.md`. 4. Discards: considered that autoload.md is a managed hub template (so its table reset is acceptable) — rejected for root `AGENTS.md` because it is explicitly documented as consumer-owned and never tool-written; considered that the gate suffices as consent — rejected because the default is Refresh and there is no authorship detection or backup.

**Caminhos analisados:** /.agents/skills/ws-configure-project/scripts/configure_autoload.py, /.agents/skills/ws-configure-project/INTERVIEW.md, /.agents/skills/ws-configure-project/SKILL.md, /.agents/skills/ws-shared/AGENTS.md, /AGENTS.md
</details>

comments.author: github-actions
comments.body:
Agentic Code Reviewer opencode

⚠️ **WARNING:** The new Autoload section's helper commands hardcode the project-local path `.agents/skills/ws-configure-project/scripts/configure_autoload.py`, while the sibling `SKILL.md` (steps 6.1 and 6.3) invokes the same helper through the portable `{skillsRoot}` token. In hybrid or global-only installs, which the harness explicitly supports (skills bodies loaded from `{globalSkillsRoot}` while the project keeps its own `ws-shared/` config), the project tree has no `.agents/skills/ws-configure-project/` directory, so an agent or test following these literal commands fails with "No such file or directory". The literal default is only copy-paste safe for project-local installs; using the token preserves `{skillsRoot}` resolution (local first, global fallback) exactly as the rest of the skill does. This is a portability inconsistency introduced in this PR that breaks the documented autoload workflow for global/hybrid consumers.

**Correção sugerida:**

```diff
- python .agents/skills/ws-configure-project/scripts/configure_autoload.py --write-autoload
- python .agents/skills/ws-configure-project/scripts/configure_autoload.py --write-root-agents
- python .agents/skills/ws-configure-project/scripts/configure_autoload.py --check --json
+ python {skillsRoot}/ws-configure-project/scripts/configure_autoload.py --write-autoload
+ python {skillsRoot}/ws-configure-project/scripts/configure_autoload.py --write-root-agents
+ python {skillsRoot}/ws-configure-project/scripts/configure_autoload.py --check --json
```

<details>
<summary>🔍 Detalhes da Análise IA</summary>

**Score:** 5/10 | **Ação dev:** fix-code

**Análise:**
1. Evidence: `INTERVIEW.md` lines 81-83 (added in this diff) use `python .agents/skills/ws-configure-project/scripts/configure_autoload.py ...`; `SKILL.md` lines 34, 57, 59 use `python {skillsRoot}/ws-configure-project/scripts/configure_autoload.py ...`; `tools.md` § Path tokens defines `{skillsRoot}` and `{globalSkillsRoot}` and rule 4 says shell recipes must expand tokens or use the literal default only when copy-paste safe; `ws-shared/AGENTS.md` documents that agents may load skill bodies from the global skills root. 2. Scenario: a consumer installed with `--global` (no project-local `.agents/skills/`), agent loads `ws-configure-project` from the global tree and follows `INTERVIEW.md`'s bash block from the consumer repo root — the literal path does not exist and the helper cannot run. 3. Protection: no fallback or note in `INTERVIEW.md` explains that the literal path assumes project-local install; the token form in `SKILL.md` resolves correctly via harness path resolution, so nothing catches the divergence. 4. Discards: considered tools.md rule 4 blessing literal default paths — rejected because that rule only applies when the default is copy-paste safe in all supported install scopes, and global/hybrid installs break it; considered treating `INTERVIEW.md` as a non-authoritative detail doc — rejected because it presents runnable commands that agents and the new eval (evals.json id 3) reference.

**Caminhos analisados:** /.agents/skills/ws-configure-project/INTERVIEW.md, /.agents/skills/ws-configure-project/SKILL.md, /.agents/skills/ws-shared/tools.md, /.agents/skills/ws-configure-project/evals/evals.json
</details>

activeThreads.summary: Agentic Code Reviewer opencode ⚠️ **WARNING:** *(Ocorrência similar identificada)* The helper derives the consumer project root from its own file location (`Path(__file__).resolve().parents[4]`) instead of the project being configured. W...

comments.author: github-actions
comments.body:
Agentic Code Reviewer opencode

⚠️ **WARNING:** *(Ocorrência similar identificada)*

The helper derives the consumer project root from its own file location (`Path(__file__).resolve().parents[4]`) instead of the project being configured. When `ws-configure-project --section autoload` runs from a global-only or hybrid install — a supported mode where `{skillsRoot}` falls back to `$HOME/.agents/skills` — that parent-4 path resolves to the user's home directory. `--write-autoload` then rewrites the machine-global hub's `autoload.md` (mutating config shared by every project), and `--write-root-agents` creates or overwrites `~/AGENTS.md`, a file outside the consumer project with no backup or create-if-missing guard. The skill's documented invocations (SKILL.md steps 6.1/6.3, INTERVIEW.md Autoload, PHASES.md helper line) never pass `--repo-root`, and the test suite always passes it, so the default derivation path is silently broken for the exact scenario the global-install feature exists to support.

**Correção sugerida:**

```python
def default_repo_root() -> Path:
    # The agent runs the helper from the consumer project root. Deriving the
    # root from __file__ breaks on global-only/hybrid installs (parents[4]
    # resolves to the user's home instead of the project).
    cwd = Path.cwd().resolve()
    if (cwd / ".agents" / "skills" / "ws-shared").is_dir():
        return cwd
    return Path(__file__).resolve().parents[4]


def _guard_project_root(repo_root: Path) -> None:
    if not (repo_root / ".agents" / "skills" / "ws-shared").is_dir():
        raise SystemExit(
            "ERROR: resolved repo root has no .agents/skills/ws-shared "
            "(global install?). Re-run with --repo-root <project root>."
        )
```
Call `_guard_project_root(repo_root)` at the top of `ensure_autoload_md()` and `write_root_agents()` so the writes fail safe instead of targeting `$HOME`. Additionally, pass `--repo-root "$PWD"` in the documented invocations in `SKILL.md` (lines 34/57/59), `INTERVIEW.md` (lines 81-83), and `PHASES.md` (line 36), and add a test case that runs the script without `--repo-root` from a project-local path.

<details>
<summary>🔍 Detalhes da Análise IA</summary>

**Score:** 7/10 | **Ação dev:** fix-code

**Análise:**
1. Evidence: `.agents/skills/ws-configure-project/scripts/configure_autoload.py` — `default_repo_root()` (lines 58-60) returns `Path(__file__).resolve().parents[4]`; `main()` (line 369) uses it whenever `--repo-root` is absent; `ensure_autoload_md()` (lines 117-118) targets `repo_root/.agents/skills/ws-shared/autoload.md`; `write_root_agents()` (lines 206-210) writes `repo_root/AGENTS.md` unconditionally (`write_text` with no backup/dry-run default). The documented invocations omit `--repo-root`: `ws-configure-project/SKILL.md` lines 34, 57, 59; `INTERVIEW.md` lines 81-83; `ws-check-harness/PHASES.md` line 36. Root `AGENTS.md` § Skill SoT/install scopes and `ws-shared/AGENTS.md` § Hybrid/override both declare `$HOME/.agents/skills` global installs a supported mode. 2. Scenario: consumer with a global-only (or hybrid, ws-configure-project absent locally) install runs `ws-configure-project --section autoload` in project P. The script at `$HOME/.agents/skills/.../configure_autoload.py` resolves repo_root to `$HOME`. `--write-autoload` rewrites `$HOME/.agents/skills/ws-shared/autoload.md` (affecting all projects on the machine); `--write-root-agents` creates or overwrites `$HOME/AGENTS.md` (data loss if the user keeps a global agent config there; stray file otherwise). The project's own `{sharedDir}/autoload.md` and root `AGENTS.md` are never written. 3. Protection: none — `test/test-autoload-configure.js` always passes explicit `--repo-root` (lines 120-126, 168-177), so the no-flag path has zero coverage; the script has no guard verifying the resolved root contains `.agents/skills/ws-shared` before writing; `write_root_agents` has no create-if-missing semantics (line 209). 4. Discards: project-local installs (`.agents/skills/...`) resolve correctly because parents[4] equals the project root — this is why the bug is silent in the common case; the user-gate (Generate/Refresh/Keep/Skip) gates intent but cannot prevent the wrong-target write once the root is mis-derived; `.agents/AGENTS.md` absence was investigated separately and is unrelated to this defect.

**Caminhos analisados:** /.agents/skills/ws-configure-project/scripts/configure_autoload.py, /.agents/skills/ws-configure-project/SKILL.md, /.agents/skills/ws-configure-project/INTERVIEW.md, /.agents/skills/ws-check-harness/PHASES.md, /test/test-autoload-configure.js
</details>
